title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (5.5%)
drivers.evidence: Historical sales at $10.81: median 31.0 vs baseline 34.7 (x0.90). Noise-adjusted estimate supports ~10% lift reduction.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 34.7. No events or promotions are planned. The price is 5.5% above regular, which historically correlates with lower sales. Recent weeks at $10.81 (same as target) show median sales of 31.0 (vs baseline 34.7), a 10.1% drop. The noise-adjusted price effect from past $10.81 weeks is x0.90. No promotion lift is expected. The classical model’s x1.00 is appropriate given no drivers. Shrink toward 1.0 due to limited evidence on price impact at this level.

brief:
PRODUCT: AA Batteries 8-pack | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.81 (+5.5% vs regular price 10.25)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 34.7 | 5%-95%: 17.5 - 59.2 | 10%-90%: 20.0 - 56.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
